scope: Audit 26 checklist commands: menu/feature route, Command Line route and produced geometry

environment.harness: om9 --mcp (same Controller as the Command Line)
environment.measurement: om9_report full projection; bounding boxes and B-Rep volume from display triangles

commands.detail: menu starts and waits for the second set; exact 500 mm3 difference is measured by solid_workflows::immediate_boolean_menu_actions_have_measured_results

checklist.evidence: snap_panel_modes + sidebar toggles; GridSnap icon disabled

Gumball Snappy follows the active osnap candidate (selected excluded); Move handles snap to the exact 3D world point; Drag strength 1-200% and a Gumball settings window (axes, Smooth/Snappy, strength, reset, defaults); 7 gumball_viewport tests
om9-scene osnap: Center on the circle
MCP row; circle split into two half arcs
MCP row; second surface at z=+-5
MCP row; 12 edge curves inside the box
MCP row Boolean Two Objects V=500; OM9-SOLID-001 menu start + solid_workflows V=500
MCP row; File/CMD/native .stl dialog + om9_export_stl; meshes, editable/retained B-Reps and surfaces; 9 stl_export tests, independent trimesh record, real Win32 save-dialog test and GPU render

supporting_tests.proves: End (10,0,0), Mid (5,0,0), Center on the circle and Quadrant candidates are exact and ranked inside the screen radius.
A viewport click inside the snap radius creates a Line whose endpoints are the exact snap world points; disabling End removes the marker; Escape clears guides.
Persistent End on/off and the one-shot override change the snap state.
Lazy layer assignment, current layer, group visibility toggle and locked-layer refusal with Undo.
The panel Hide and Show buttons change object visibility and keep explicit hidden/selectable preferences.
The panel and the model agree on the current layer and assignment.
A real widget drag on a gumball arrow moves the selected line and commits one transform.
OM9-SOLID-001 Difference through the menu and the object pick yields volume 500 mm3 and one Undo transaction.
The STL writer itself is correct (closed cube layout, units, winding, refusals); it is not connected to the application.
Dispatching OM9-TOP11-006 starts the same Move pending state and geometry as the toolbar icon.
Typed Cancel ends Sphere/Box/Cylinder/Cone prompts without a document mutation.
No Top11 regression after adding feature-id dispatch.
No solid regression after the shared Cancel branch.
Top11Action::from_feature is additive in the core crate.
The MCP protocol surface and the om9_export_stl tool work after the dispatch change.
Menu/CMD routes, selection, mixed skip, sphere watertightness, retained native payload re-import, adaptive open surface, units, wrong extension and atomic replace.
Select/drag/rotate/scale, typed Snappy/Smooth, exact 3D snap, drag strength 50% and bounded settings/defaults.
The settings window renders and typed settings persist through the application-scope file and reload.
A real Win32 pointer drag on the live wgpu window lands the line on the 3D snap point and saves the GPU framebuffer.
The real Windows Save dialog with the .stl filter, owned HWND and IDOK probe returns the chosen audit.stl path.
A third-party library (not the OM9 writer) confirms box/sphere triangle counts, mm bounds, volumes, watertightness, winding and no degenerate faces.
om9 --render-4 draws the box and sphere in all four viewports; PNG 1280x800, sha256 040ae890...a643da1.

findings.before: om9_dispatch(OM9-TOP11-006) returned 'unsupported command has no accepted standalone operation'; only the toolbar and typed name reached the action.
findings.after: Top11Action::from_feature + dispatch_effect route the published id through top11_invoke, the same function the toolbar calls.
findings.evidence: tests/top11.rs::feature_dispatch_reaches_the_same_action_as_the_toolbar; MCP menu column PASS for all six Top11 rows.

findings.before: Sphere/Box/Cylinder/Cone advertised Cancel but typing it returned errors such as 'sphere center needs three coordinates'.
findings.after: submit_solid_pending handles Cancel/Esc once before any feature handler.
findings.evidence: tests/solid.rs::typed_cancel_ends_a_solid_prompt_without_mutation; MCP probe shows running=false for all four.

Controller::export_stl_selected handles selected meshes, editable OCCT B-Reps (shared re-tessellation), retained NativeBrep payloads (OCCT bridge, not display) and NurbsSurfaces (adaptive 8-128 chord grid); applies placement, welds nodes, drops pole degenerates, writes strict when closed and non-strict with open_edges for surfaces, atomically in mm. FileExportSelected, typed ExportSTL and MCP om9_export_stl share it; the real Win32 .stl dialog test passes. Independent trimesh read-back confirms box/sphere counts, bounds, volume, watertightness, winding and no degenerates.

Snappy uses the active osnap candidates during a drag, excluding the moved objects; Move handles use the exact world candidate through Drag::WorldDelta while axis/plane handles keep their constraints. Drag strength (1-200%) scales smooth pointer motion, and a Gumball settings window covers World/Object/CPlane, Smooth/Snappy, strength, reset pivot and defaults. Snappy/strength/alignment persist in %APPDATA%/OpenMatrix9/gumball.json and reload at startup. A real OS-mouse drag on the wgpu window (tools/gumball-os-audit.ps1) lands a line on the 3D snap point and records the GPU screenshot.
Per-kind object snaps (End/Mid/Center/...) and Ortho/Planar/Project toggles work. GridSnapON and the header GridSnap icon stay visible but disabled: no grid-snap model exists.

Connected through the Layers panel (arrow assigns, visibility/lock controls, Hide/Show buttons); there is no typed Assign/Hide/Show command. The typed Layer command sets the current layer or creates its preset group.
